headline.title: First flakes for Northern Vermont.
headline.text: Up to {{s:2.8}} on the summit of Jay Peak Sunday evening to Monday afternoon, and {{s:6.5}} for the week. None of the resorts close to opening get cold enough to make snow this week. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Periods of scattered showers will continue this afternoon through the upcoming weekend as temperatures cool to near normal levels.
There will be additional opportunities for non-impactful, beneficial precipitation during the early to middle portion of next week as the pattern remains unsettled.

ALY.excerpt:
) Low to medium chances for rain showers tomorrow for locations south and east of Albany, with no flooding impacts expected.
) Medium to high chances for rain showers Saturday across eastern New York and western New England, with no flooding impacts expected. Temperatures trend near normal early next week.

GYX.excerpt: Two rounds of rain are expected to bring beneficial rainfall Friday through Saturday night with heaviest amounts expected for the immediate coast with lighter amounts for mountains.

BUF.excerpt:
) Breezy conditions and above normal temperatures continue through this evening.
) Unsettled weather and cooler temperatures Friday through the weekend.

PHI.excerpt: A slow moving cold front approaches tonight and crosses the area Friday.

CTP.excerpt:
) Unseasonably mild through Friday with 2.5 weeks-long dry spell now over.
) Trending cooler this weekend with lake enhanced rain showers beneath upper level low

RLX.excerpt:
) A few showers possible east of I-79 tomorrow evening as the reinforcing cold front crosses.
) Much cooler temperatures for the weekend bring frost/freeze concerns across our counties that still have an active growing season.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Some snow early Monday, best at Smugglers' Notch.
paras: Light snow early Monday to Monday afternoon: Smugglers' Notch {{s:3}}, Stowe {{s:3}}, Jay Peak {{s:2.8}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.6,5.3}} at Smugglers' Notch. It's a northwest upslope setup, one that usually favors Smugglers' Notch, Stowe and Jay Peak. Rain mixes in at the bases.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:39}} to {{t:57}}, with rain at times.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Nights stay too mild to make much snow this week.
Trend: totals have gone up since yesterday, led by Jay Peak ({{s:1.8}} to {{s:5}}).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Thursday 2:28 PM: "Periods of scattered showers will continue this afternoon through the upcoming weekend as temperatures cool to near normal levels."

writeups.title: Just a coating for the high peaks.
paras: Light snow Saturday afternoon to Sunday morning: Cannon {{s:1.6}}, Waterville Valley {{s:0.5}} at the summits, though the models range from {{r:0.4,4.6}} at Cannon. Rain mixes in even up high at times.
Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:43}} to {{t:61}}, with rain at times.
Bretton Woods usually opens first here, around Nov 15. Nights stay too mild to make much snow this week.
Trend: totals have gone up since yesterday, led by Cannon ({{s:1.3}} to {{s:3.8}}).

NWS Gray forecasters, Thursday 3:27 PM: "Two rounds of rain are expected to bring beneficial rainfall Friday through Saturday night with heaviest amounts expected for the immediate coast with lighter amounts for mountains."

insights.text: First flakes: about {{s:2.8}} at the summit Sunday evening to Monday afternoon (models {{r:0.9,5.8}}). Snow level near {{e:2800}}, so the base ({{e:1800}}) mixes with or changes to rain Sunday evening: about {{s:0}} there vs {{s:2.8}} up top. Highs stay near {{t:36}} afterward, so some of it should stick up high.
Too mild to make snow this week: mid-mountain doesn't stay at or below {{t:26}} (counting humidity) for long.
Typically opens around Nov 27, 22 days out.
